newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos says peso level reasonable.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos says peso level reasonable.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Monday the present level of the peso was reasonable.

"The last report I heard...(the peso) was at 28.20 which is very reasonable and well below the predictions of some doomsayers, some of them well-known economists and national leaders," he told reporters.
The peso's weighted average is now 28.772 to the dollar.
"It closed at 29. It's still okay as far as we're concerned," Ramos added.
The peso touched an almost four-year low of 29.75 this morning following last Friday's move by the central bank to widen the currency's trading band.
It regained some ground by the close after the central bank sold dollars, traders said.

"What is important is for the public through our government officials and leaders of the ngos (non-government organisations) to know is the impact of all this on prices, labour, wages, on the foreign debt as well as all implications on the common man," Ramos said.
The government had been working since Saturday to make sure that stability of prices would be maintained," he added.
